BRM feature atlas ​

Every executable example in the user guide has the same four semantic views: the BRM declaration, the StanBlocks model BRM emitted, the complete Stan source emitted from that model, and the Turing model selected directly from the BRM. Choose a tab for one view, or Compare and select any two or more views for a side-by-side reading. If a backend does not support an example, its pane remains present and shows the exact construction error produced by the current build.

Nothing below is copied output. The docs build evaluates the displayed source and derives all three emission panes from it.

Gaussian population model and effect priors ​

brm-comparison
Gaussian population model
julia
gaussian = (@brm begin
    sigma ~ Exponential(2)
    mu ~ 1 + x
    effect(:, :) ~ Normal(0, 2)
    effect(mu, x) ~ Normal(0, 0.25)
    y ~ Normal(mu, sigma)
end)((; x=[-1.0, 0.5, 2.0], y=[0.2, 1.1, -0.4]))
julia
BRMI:
  sigma ~ Exponential(2)
  x: data (eltype=Float64, n=3)
  mu ~ 1 + x
  effect(:, :) ~ Normal(0, 2)
  effect(mu, x) ~ Normal(0, 0.25)
  y ~ Normal(mu, sigma)
julia
SBBRMI with data keys = [:x, :y]
emitted @slic body:
begin
    sigma ~ exponential(1.0 ./ 2)
    X_mu = hcat(rep_vector(1.0, num_elements(x)), x)
    pop_mu ~ _popefs_normal_coefs(; X = X_mu, beta_loc = [0, 0], beta_scale = [2, 0.25])
    y ~ normal_id_glm(X_mu, 0.0, pop_mu, sigma)
    mu = X_mu * pop_mu
end
stan
functions {
matrix hcat(
    vector x,
    vector y
) {
    int n = dims(x)[1];
    if (dims(y)[1] != n) reject("hcat: dim mismatch — `y` dim 1 (= ", dims(y)[1], ") does not match `n` (= ", n, "), inferred from `x` dim 1. `n` sizes: `x` dim 1 (= ", dims(x)[1], "), `y` dim 1 (= ", dims(y)[1], ").");
    return append_col(x, y);
}
vector normal_id_glm_lpdfs(
    vector y,
    matrix X,
    real alpha,
    vector beta,
    real sigma
) {
    int n = dims(y)[1];
    if (dims(X)[1] != n) reject("normal_id_glm_lpdfs: dim mismatch — `X` dim 1 (= ", dims(X)[1], ") does not match `n` (= ", n, "), inferred from `y` dim 1. `n` sizes: `y` dim 1 (= ", dims(y)[1], "), `X` dim 1 (= ", dims(X)[1], ").");
    vector[n] rv;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        rv[i] = normal_lpdf(y[i] | (alpha + (X[i, :] * beta)), sigma);
    }
    return rv;
}
vector normal_id_glm_vector_rng(
    int anontok__1,
    matrix X,
    real alpha,
    vector beta,
    real sigma
) {
    int m = anontok__1;
    if (dims(X)[1] != m) reject("normal_id_glm_rng: dim mismatch — `X` dim 1 (= ", dims(X)[1], ") does not match `m` (= ", m, "), inferred from `anontok__1` dim 1. `m` sizes: `anontok__1` dim 1 (= ", anontok__1, "), `X` dim 1 (= ", dims(X)[1], ").");
    if((m == 0)) {
        vector[m] rv;
        return rv;
    } else {
        return normal_id_glm_rng(X, alpha, beta, sigma);
    }
}
vector normal_id_glm_rng(
    matrix X,
    real alpha,
    vector beta,
    real sigma
) {
    int m = dims(X)[1];
    if((m == 0)) {
        vector[m] rv;
        return rv;
    } else {
        return to_vector(normal_rng((rep_vector(alpha, m) + (X * beta)), sigma));
    }
}
}
data {
    int x_n;
    vector[x_n] x;
    int y_n;
    vector[y_n] y;
}
transformed data {
    matrix[x_n, 2] X_mu = hcat(rep_vector(1.0, num_elements(x)), x);
    int pop_mu_n_covariates = 2;
}
parameters {
    real<lower=0.0> sigma;
    vector[pop_mu_n_covariates] pop_mu_beta_pop;
}
transformed parameters {
    vector[pop_mu_n_covariates] pop_mu = pop_mu_beta_pop;
}
model {
    sigma ~ exponential((1.0 ./ 2));
    pop_mu_beta_pop ~ normal([0, 0]', [2, 0.25]');
    y ~ normal_id_glm(X_mu, 0.0, pop_mu, sigma);
}
generated quantities {
    vector[x_n] y_likelihood = normal_id_glm_lpdfs(y, X_mu, 0.0, pop_mu, sigma);
    vector[x_n] y_gen = normal_id_glm_vector_rng(y_n, X_mu, 0.0, pop_mu, sigma);
    vector[x_n] mu = (X_mu * pop_mu);
}
julia
#= line 0 =# Turing.@model(function brm_model(y, X_mu)
        sigma ~ Distributions.Exponential(2)

        eta_mu = X_mu * beta_pop

functions {
matrix hcat(
    vector x,
    vector y
) {
    int n = dims(x)[1];
    if (dims(y)[1] != n) reject("hcat: dim mismatch — `y` dim 1 (= ", dims(y)[1], ") does not match `n` (= ", n, "), inferred from `x` dim 1. `n` sizes: `x` dim 1 (= ", dims(x)[1], "), `y` dim 1 (= ", dims(y)[1], ").");
    return append_col(x, y);
}
vector normal_vector_rng(

) {

    if((n == 0)) {

vector normal_lpdfs(

vector jbroadcasted_normal_lpdfs(
    vector x1,
    vector x2,

) {
    int n = dims(x1)[1];
    vector[n] rv;

real normal_lpdfs(
    real args1,

    return x[i];

vector mi_merge(
    vector y_obs,
    vector y_mis,
    array[] int Jobs,
    array[] int Jmis,
    int n
) {
    int n_obs = dims(y_obs)[1];
    int n_mis = dims(y_mis)[1];
    if (dims(Jobs)[1] != n_obs) reject("mi_merge: dim mismatch — `Jobs` dim 1 (= ", dims(Jobs)[1], ") does not match `n_obs` (= ", n_obs, "), inferred from `y_obs` dim 1. `n_obs` sizes: `y_obs` dim 1 (= ", dims(y_obs)[1], "), `Jobs` dim 1 (= ", dims(Jobs)[1], ").");
    if (dims(Jmis)[1] != n_mis) reject("mi_merge: dim mismatch — `Jmis` dim 1 (= ", dims(Jmis)[1], ") does not match `n_mis` (= ", n_mis, "), inferred from `y_mis` dim 1. `n_mis` sizes: `y_mis` dim 1 (= ", dims(y_mis)[1], "), `Jmis` dim 1 (= ", dims(Jmis)[1], ").");
    vector[n] rv = rep_vector(0.0, n);
    if((n_obs > 0)) {
        for(i in 1:n_obs) {
            rv[Jobs[i]] = y_obs[i];
        }
    }
    if((n_mis > 0)) {
        for(i in 1:n_mis) {
            rv[Jmis[i]] = y_mis[i];
        }
    }
    return rv;
}
}
data {
    int x_n;
    vector[x_n] x;
    int Jmis_y_n;
    array[Jmis_y_n] int Jmis_y;
    int y_obs_n;
    vector[y_obs_n] y_obs;
    int Jobs_y_n;
    array[Jobs_y_n] int Jobs_y;
}
transformed data {
    matrix[x_n, 2] X_mu = hcat(rep_vector(1.0, num_elements(x)), x);
    int pop_mu_n_covariates = 2;
    int y_n_mis = num_elements(Jmis_y);
}
parameters {
    real<lower=0.0> sigma;
    vector[pop_mu_n_covariates] pop_mu_beta_pop;
}
transformed parameters {
    vector[x_n] pop_mu = (X_mu * pop_mu_beta_pop);
    vector[x_n] mu = pop_mu;
}
model {
    sigma ~ exponential((1.0 ./ 2));
    pop_mu_beta_pop ~ std_normal();
    y_obs ~ normal(mu[Jobs_y], sigma);
}
generated quantities {
    vector[y_n_mis] y_y_mis = normal_vector_rng(y_n_mis, mu[Jmis_y], sigma);
    vector[y_obs_n] y_obs_likelihood = normal_lpdfs(y_obs, mu[Jobs_y], sigma);
    vector[y_obs_n] y_obs_gen = normal_vector_rng(y_obs_n, mu[Jobs_y], sigma);
    vector[(num_elements(Jobs_y) + y_n_mis)] y = mi_merge(y_obs, y_y_mis, Jobs_y, Jmis_y, (num_elements(Jobs_y) + y_n_mis));
}

Shared and independent multi-response model ​

brm-comparison
Shared and independent responses
julia
multi_response = (@brm begin
    sigma ~ Exponential(2)
    mu ~ 1 + x
    y ~ Normal(mu, sigma)

    log(rate) ~ 1 + z
    count ~ Poisson(rate)

    y_replicate ~ Normal(mu, sigma)
end)((;
    x=[-1.0, 0.5, 2.0],
    z=[0.25, -0.5, 1.0],
    y=[0.2, 1.1, -0.4],
    count=[0, 2, 4],
    y_replicate=[-0.1, 0.3, 0.7],
))
julia

  log(rate) ~ 1 + z

begin
    sigma ~ exponential(1.0 ./ 2)
    X_mu = hcat(rep_vector(1.0, num_elements(x)), x)
    pop_mu ~ popefs(; X = X_mu)
    mu = pop_mu
    y ~ normal(mu, sigma)
    X_log_rate = hcat(rep_vector(1.0, num_elements(z)), z)
    pop_log_rate ~ popefs(; X = X_log_rate)

end

#= line 0 =# Turing.@model(function brm_multi_model(y_1, y_2, y_3, X_mu, X_rate)
        sigma ~ Distributions.Exponential(2)
        beta_pop_mu ~ Distributions.product_distribution(Base.fill(Distributions.Normal(), 2))
        eta_mu = X_mu * beta_pop_mu
        mu = eta_mu
        beta_pop_rate ~ Distributions.product_distribution(Base.fill(Distributions.Normal(), 2))
        eta_rate = X_rate * beta_pop_rate
        rate = Base.exp.(eta_rate)
        begin
            for i = Base.eachindex(y_1)
                y_1[i] ~ Distributions.Normal(mu[i], sigma)
            end
        end
        begin
            for i = Base.eachindex(y_2)
                y_2[i] ~ Distributions.Poisson(rate[i])
            end
        end
        begin
            for i = Base.eachindex(y_3)
                y_3[i] ~ Distributions.Normal(mu[i], sigma)
            end
        end
        (; responses = ((; mu = mu, rate = rate, sigma = sigma, response = y_1), (; mu = mu, rate = rate, sigma = sigma, response = y_2), (; mu = mu, rate = rate, sigma = sigma, response = y_3)))
    end)

Correlated Gaussian multi-response model ​

The vector response is one row-wise multivariate likelihood. Outcome order is the order written on both sides, and L_res is the estimated residual covariance Cholesky factor (marginal scales plus an LKJ correlation factor).

brm-comparison
Correlated Gaussian responses
julia
correlated_response = (@brm begin
    L_res ~ LKJCovarianceFactor(
        2; scale_prior=Exponential(1), shape=2,
    )
    shared_log_rate ~ Normal(0, 1)
    concentration_mu = exp(-exp(shared_log_rate) * time)
    effect_mu = 1.0 - concentration_mu
    [concentration, effect] ~ MvNormalCholesky(
        [concentration_mu, effect_mu], L_res)
end)((;
    time=[0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0],
    concentration=[1.0, 0.72, 0.51, 0.27],
    effect=[0.03, 0.18, 0.43, 0.79],
))
julia
BRMI:
  L_res ~ LKJCovarianceFactor(2; scale_prior=Exponential(1), shape=2)
  shared_log_rate ~ Normal(0, 1)
  time: data (eltype=Float64, n=4)
  :concentration_mu = exp((-(exp(shared_log_rate)) * time))
  :effect_mu = -(1.0, concentration_mu)
  [concentration, effect] ~ MvNormalCholesky(NamedColumn{Symbol}[concentration_mu, effect_mu], L_res)
julia
SBBRMI with data keys = [:L_res_n, :brm_joint_concentration__effect_n, :brm_joint_concentration__effect_observed, :time]
emitted @slic body:
begin
    L_res_scales ~ exponential(1.0; n = L_res_n)
    L_res_L_corr::cholesky_factor_corr[L_res_n] ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2.0)
    L_res = diag_pre_multiply(L_res_scales, L_res_L_corr)
    shared_log_rate ~ normal(0, 1)
    concentration_mu = (exp)((-)((exp)(shared_log_rate)) .* time)
    effect_mu = (-)(1.0, concentration_mu)
    brm_joint_concentration__effect_means ~ plate(brm_joint_concentration__effect_observed, concentration_mu, effect_mu; outer = (brm_joint_concentration__effect_n,)) do brm_joint_concentration__effect_observed_cell, brm_joint_concentration__effect_mean_cell_1, brm_joint_concentration__effect_mean_cell_2
            brm_joint_concentration__effect_mean_vector = 0.0 .* brm_joint_concentration__effect_observed_cell + [brm_joint_concentration__effect_mean_cell_1, brm_joint_concentration__effect_mean_cell_2]
            brm_joint_concentration__effect_mean_vector
        end
    brm_joint_concentration__effect_observed ~ multi_normal_cholesky(brm_joint_concentration__effect_means, L_res)
end

Shared distributional group covariance ​

The repeated joint ID makes the mean and precision slopes slices of one four-dimensional covariance block for each subject. Removing the ID would make the two predictor blocks independent.

        eta_phi = eta_phi + shared_group_1.effects[2]

Multi-axis population PK kernel ​

The subject frame has one row per person, while the observation frame has one row per concentration measurement. Those axes deliberately have different lengths and the observation rows are interleaved. ragged(x, group) joins the flat observation columns to the subject axis; kernel(...) then evaluates one structural-model cell per subject. In the generated StanBlocks pane, that public BRM kernel lowers to a plate.

This is a deliberately small one-compartment IV-bolus model, C(t) = dose / V * exp(-(CL / V)t). The shared pk ID gives CL and V one correlated between-subject variability block.

brm-comparison
Multi-axis population PK kernel
julia
population_pk = (@brm begin
    sigma ~ Exponential(1)
    log(CL) ~ 1 + (1 | pk | subject)
    log(V)  ~ 1 + (1 | pk | subject)

    predicted_concentration ~ kernel(
        ragged(time, obs_subject), dose, CL, V,
    ) do ts, d, cl, volume
        d / volume * exp((-cl / volume) * ts)
    end

    ragged(concentration, obs_subject) ~
        Normal(predicted_concentration, sigma)
end)((;
    # Subject axis: one row per subject.
    subject=["alice", "bob"],
    dose=[100.0, 80.0],

    # Observation axis: one row per sample, interleaved by subject.
    obs_subject=["alice", "bob", "alice", "bob", "alice"],
    time=[0.5, 0.25, 1.5, 1.0, 3.0],
    concentration=[8.1, 7.6, 5.2, 4.9, 2.1],
))

Verified public Warfarin PK/PD reproduction ​

The repository includes a complete executable translation of Sebastian Weber's public StanCon 2018 Warfarin programs: a first-stage one-compartment oral PK model with lag, allometry, four independent subject effects, and Gamma overdispersion; followed by a turnover PD ODE conditioned on the public PK posterior medians, with three independent PD subject effects and the same observation family.

The reproduction script contains the typed ODE and likelihood definitions, a public two-subject data slice, both @brm declarations, stanc checks, and finite BridgeStan density and gradient checks. The accompanying audit notes map every retained prior, structural equation, solver tolerance, and known generated-quantity difference back to the public source.

The Warfarin PK/PD page also renders the separately specified joint model: one posterior in which shared subject-level PK effects feed both the PK and PD likelihoods, so PK uncertainty propagates into PD and PD data can update PK quantities.

julia
include("research/warfarin/reproduce.jl")
models = warfarin_sbbrmis()

This is the strongest identifiable public match to the Warfarin model mentioned in brms issue #1509, but the issue itself provides no equations or citation, so identity with the commenter's private working model cannot be proved. The public StanCon model is two separate scalar-Gamma stages; it does not need the correlated Gaussian outcome surface above.

Random-effect scale and correlation priors ​

The p identifier gives the group block a stable prior address. The shared half-Normal sets both scales, then the more-specific Exponential override replaces it only on the x margin.

brm-comparison
Addressed group scale and correlation priors
julia
grouped_priors = (@brm begin
    sigma ~ Exponential(2)
    mu ~ 1 + x + (1 + x | p | subject)
    sd(:, p) ~ Normal(0, 0.5)
    sd(mu, p, x) ~ Exponential(0.25)
    cor(:, p) ~ LKJCholesky(2, 2.5)
    outcome ~ Normal(mu, sigma)
end)((;
    x=[-1.0, 0.5, 2.0, 0.25],
    subject=[2, 1, 2, 3],
    outcome=[0.2, 1.1, -0.4, 0.7],
))

real brm_vector_prior_5cc114893928eff4_lpdf(
    vector x,
    real arg_1,

) {

    if((x[2] < 0.0)) {

Stratified group covariance ​

gr(subject, by=arm) fits a separate scale/correlation frame in each arm while retaining one pooled subject coordinate.

brm-comparison
Group covariance stratified by arm

stratified_groups = (@brm begin
    sigma ~ Exponential(2)
    mu ~ 1 + x + (1 + x | gr(subject, by=arm))
    outcome ~ Normal(mu, sigma)

Multi-membership group effects ​

Each row belongs to two groups. The row weights are normalized before the two group contributions are pooled; normalize=false is the explicit raw-weight variant.

brm-comparison
Weighted multi-membership random slopes

    g1=[1, 1, 2, 3],

    w2=[1.0, 1.0, 1.5, 1.0],

functions {
matrix hcat(
    vector x,
    vector y
) {
    int n = dims(x)[1];
    if (dims(y)[1] != n) reject("hcat: dim mismatch — `y` dim 1 (= ", dims(y)[1], ") does not match `n` (= ", n, "), inferred from `x` dim 1. `n` sizes: `x` dim 1 (= ", dims(x)[1], "), `y` dim 1 (= ", dims(y)[1], ").");
    return append_col(x, y);
}
vector multi_membership_correlated(
    matrix Z,
    matrix b,
    array[] int group_idx,
    vector weights,
    int n_obs,
    int n_memberships
) {
    int n_terms = dims(Z)[2];
    int n_mm = dims(group_idx)[1];
    if (dims(b)[2] != n_terms) reject("multi_membership_correlated: dim mismatch — `b` dim 2 (= ", dims(b)[2], ") does not match `n_terms` (= ", n_terms, "), inferred from `Z` dim 2. `n_terms` sizes: `Z` dim 2 (= ", dims(Z)[2], "), `b` dim 2 (= ", dims(b)[2], ").");
    if (dims(weights)[1] != n_mm) reject("multi_membership_correlated: dim mismatch — `weights` dim 1 (= ", dims(weights)[1], ") does not match `n_mm` (= ", n_mm, "), inferred from `group_idx` dim 1. `n_mm` sizes: `group_idx` dim 1 (= ", dims(group_idx)[1], "), `weights` dim 1 (= ", dims(weights)[1], ").");
    vector[n_obs] rv = rep_vector(0.0, n_obs);
    for(i in 1:n_obs) {
        for(m in 1:n_memberships) {
            int j = (((i - 1) * n_memberships) + m);
            for(k in 1:n_terms) {
                rv[i] += (weights[j] * Z[i, k] * b[group_idx[j], k]);
            }
        }
    }
    return rv;
}

    vector y,

    vector x1,

real interval_evidence_impl_normal_lpdf(
    real y,
    real lo,

    real args1,
    real args2
) {
    array[1] real rv;

) {
